answer: The falcon report reveals the merge explicitly at each raven. The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. Because of that, an attacker who spins up 94 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 10 times the capital for one share. Each copy needs 2 hours of work. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
